## Causal Forest with Simulated Data

Simulates heterogeneous effects and plots estimated CATEs, pointwise intervals, and the known CATE.

```{r}
library(grf)
library(DiagrammeR)

set.seed(5280)
n <- 3000
p <- 12
W <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
D <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4 + 0.2 * (W[, 1] > 0))
Y <- pmax(W[, 1], 0) * D + W[, 2] + pmin(W[, 3], 0) + rnorm(n)

W_test <- matrix(0, nrow = 101, ncol = p)
W_test[, 1] <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 101)


forest_full <- causal_forest(W, Y, D, num.trees = 4000)
plot(get_tree(forest_full, 1)) # visualize one of the 4000 trees. Unnecessary for estimation.

pred <- predict(forest_full, W_test, estimate.variance = TRUE)
se <- sqrt(pred$variance.estimates)

plot(W_test[, 1], pred$predictions,
     ylim = range(pred$predictions - 1.96 * se,
                  pred$predictions + 1.96 * se, 0, 2),
     xlab = expression(W[1]), ylab = "CATE", type = "l")
lines(W_test[, 1], pred$predictions + 1.96 * se, lty = 2)
lines(W_test[, 1], pred$predictions - 1.96 * se, lty = 2)
lines(W_test[, 1], pmax(W_test[, 1], 0), col = 2)
legend("topleft", c("forest", "95% pointwise interval", "truth"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 1), col = c(1, 1, 2), bty = "n")
```

## Welfare CATEs by Education

Fits a causal forest to welfare-small.csv and plots CATE estimates across education at age 30.

```{r}
data <- read.csv("data/welfare-small.csv")
n <- nrow(data)
Y=as.numeric(data$Y)
D=as.numeric(data$D)
W=cbind(data$age,data$educ)


## Generate values of interest for w
W.test <- cbind(30,seq(min(data$educ),max(data$educ),by=1))

### Build a causal forest.
tau.forest <- causal_forest(W, Y, D) # Put regressors
tree <- get_tree(tau.forest, 1)
plot(tree) # visualize the first tree in the forest

# Estimate treatment effects with pointwise confidence intervals
tau.forest <- causal_forest(W, Y, D, num.trees = 4000)
tau.hat <- predict(tau.forest, W.test, estimate.variance = TRUE)
sigma.hat <- sqrt(tau.hat$variance.estimates)
plot(W.test[, 2], tau.hat$predictions, ylim =
       range(tau.hat$predictions + 1.96 * sigma.hat, 
             tau.hat$predictions - 1.96 * sigma.hat), 
     xlab = "educ", ylab = "CATE", type = "l")
lines(W.test[, 2], tau.hat$predictions + 1.96 * sigma.hat, col = 1, lty = 2)
lines(W.test[, 2], tau.hat$predictions - 1.96 * sigma.hat, col = 1, lty = 2)
```
